rules.title: Stimulant with an MAO inhibitor
rules.effect: Risk of hypertensive crisis.
rules.management: Do not combine. Stimulant labels contraindicate use during or within 14 days after stopping an MAOI. (The ONC panel notes low-dose selegiline is MAO-B selective.)

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)

rules.title: Atazanavir with a proton pump inhibitor
rules.effect: PPIs sharply reduce atazanavir absorption, risking loss of virologic response and resistance.
rules.management: Avoid the combination; follow the atazanavir label for the narrow exceptions.

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)

rules.title: Febuxostat with azathioprine or mercaptopurine
rules.effect: Xanthine oxidase inhibition raises thiopurine levels and can cause severe bone-marrow suppression.
rules.management: Contraindicated per the febuxostat label.

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)

rules.title: Serotonergic drug with an MAO inhibitor
rules.effect: Risk of serotonin syndrome (agitation, hyperthermia, clonus, autonomic instability), which can be fatal. Linezolid and methylene blue also inhibit MAO.
rules.management: Do not combine. Labels require a washout (generally 14 days; 5 weeks after fluoxetine).

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)
FDA label: linezolid, Warnings and Precautions

rules.title: Irinotecan with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor
rules.effect: Raises exposure to irinotecan's active metabolite, with severe diarrhea and neutropenia.
rules.management: Avoid; the irinotecan label advises stopping strong CYP3A4 inhibitors at least 1 week before therapy.

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)

rules.title: Opioid with an MAO inhibitor
rules.effect: Risk of serotonin syndrome or opioid toxicity (respiratory depression, coma).
rules.management: Avoid. The meperidine and tramadol labels contraindicate use with or within 14 days of an MAOI; the methadone label says use with MAOIs is not recommended.

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)

rules.title: Tricyclic antidepressant with an MAO inhibitor
rules.effect: Risk of serotonin syndrome and hypertensive reactions.
rules.management: Do not combine; observe the label washout periods.

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)

rules.title: Two drugs whose FDA labels warn of QT prolongation
rules.effect: Additive QT prolongation with a risk of torsades de pointes and sudden cardiac death.
rules.management: Avoid the combination where possible. If both are needed, get a baseline ECG, correct potassium and magnesium, and monitor the QTc.

sources.label: ONC high-priority pair: QT-prolonging agents (Phansalkar 2012). ONC defines this class by the torsades.org high-risk list, which needs a licence; this demo uses drugs whose FDA labels warn of QT prolongation or torsades de pointes
FDA label: amiodarone, Warnings and Precautions
FDA label: azithromycin, Warnings and Precautions: QT prolongation

rules.title: Ramelteon with a strong CYP1A2 inhibitor
rules.effect: Markedly higher ramelteon levels and excess sedation.
rules.management: Avoid; the ramelteon label says not to use with fluvoxamine.

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)

rules.title: Strong CYP3A4 inducer with a protease inhibitor
rules.effect: Loss of antiviral effect and risk of resistance.
rules.management: Do not combine; check the antiviral's label for contraindicated inducers.

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)

rules.title: Simvastatin or lovastatin with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor
rules.effect: Large rise in statin levels: myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
rules.management: Contraindicated per the simvastatin label (clarithromycin, erythromycin, azole antifungals, HIV protease inhibitors, cyclosporine and others). Hold the statin during a short antibiotic course or choose a non-interacting antibiotic.

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)

rules.title: Ergot alkaloid with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor
rules.effect: Ergotism: severe vasospasm with limb or cerebral ischemia (boxed warning).
rules.management: Contraindicated (ergotamine and dihydroergotamine boxed warnings name protease inhibitors and macrolide antibiotics).

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)

rules.title: Tizanidine with a CYP1A2 inhibitor
rules.effect: Tizanidine levels rise many-fold: severe hypotension, bradycardia and sedation.
rules.management: Contraindicated with ciprofloxacin and fluvoxamine; avoid other CYP1A2 inhibitors such as amiodarone and propafenone (tizanidine label).

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)

rules.title: Tranylcypromine with procarbazine
rules.effect: Additive MAO inhibition: hypertensive crisis.
rules.management: Do not combine.

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)

rules.title: Triptan with an MAO inhibitor
rules.effect: MAO-A inhibitors raise sumatriptan, rizatriptan and zolmitriptan levels; serotonin toxicity.
rules.management: Contraindicated (triptan labels).

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)

rules.title: Anticoagulant with an NSAID
rules.effect: Higher risk of serious bleeding, especially gastrointestinal.
rules.management: Monitor closely for bleeding (anticoagulant labels: NSAIDs increase bleeding risk). Acetaminophen is usually preferred for pain; if an NSAID is needed, use the lowest dose for the shortest time, consider GI protection, and check the INR with warfarin.

sources.label: FDA label: ibuprofen, Warnings and Precautions: bleeding

rules.title: Anticoagulant with an antiplatelet
rules.effect: Additive bleeding risk.
rules.management: Confirm there is a current indication for both and how long the combination should last.

rules.title: Anticoagulant with an SSRI or SNRI
rules.effect: SSRIs and SNRIs impair platelet function and add to bleeding risk.
rules.management: Monitor for bleeding.

sources.label: FDA label: sertraline, Warnings and Precautions: abnormal bleeding

rules.title: Antiplatelet with an NSAID
rules.effect: Higher risk of GI bleeding; ibuprofen can blunt aspirin's antiplatelet effect.
rules.management: Avoid regular NSAID use where possible; if needed, consider GI protection. With low-dose aspirin, take ibuprofen at least 30 minutes after immediate-release aspirin or 8 hours before.

rules.title: NSAID with an SSRI or SNRI
rules.effect: Increased risk of GI bleeding.
rules.management: Consider GI protection for longer courses.

sources.label: FDA label: sertraline, Warnings and Precautions: abnormal bleeding

rules.title: Warfarin with an azole antifungal
rules.effect: Azoles (notably fluconazole) inhibit warfarin metabolism: INR rise and bleeding.
rules.management: Avoid if possible; otherwise check INR within a few days of starting and adjust warfarin.

rules.title: Warfarin with amiodarone
rules.effect: Amiodarone inhibits warfarin metabolism; the INR rises over weeks.
rules.management: Monitor INR closely when starting or changing amiodarone; warfarin doses usually need reducing.

rules.title: Warfarin with sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim
rules.effect: CYP2C9 inhibition raises the INR; bleeding risk.
rules.management: Prefer another antibiotic if possible; otherwise check INR within 3–5 days.

rules.title: Warfarin with metronidazole
rules.effect: Metronidazole inhibits warfarin metabolism: INR rise and bleeding.
rules.management: Avoid if possible; otherwise monitor INR closely.

rules.title: Warfarin with clarithromycin or erythromycin
rules.effect: Both inhibit CYP3A4 and can raise the INR; bleeding risk (warfarin label, drug interactions table).
rules.management: Prefer another antibiotic if reasonable; otherwise check the INR within a few days of starting and after stopping.

rules.title: Warfarin with a fluoroquinolone
rules.effect: Fluoroquinolones can raise the INR.
rules.management: Check INR during the course.

rules.title: Anticoagulant with a strong enzyme inducer
rules.effect: Lower anticoagulant levels and loss of stroke or clot protection.
rules.management: DOAC labels advise avoiding combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort); with warfarin, monitor INR closely.

rules.title: Apixaban or rivaroxaban with a combined strong CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitor
rules.effect: Higher anticoagulant levels and bleeding risk.
rules.management: Follow the DOAC label: rivaroxaban, avoid; apixaban, the label calls for a dose change or avoidance depending on the current dose.

sources.label: FDA label: apixaban, Dosage and Administration

rules.title: Clopidogrel with omeprazole or esomeprazole
rules.effect: These PPIs inhibit CYP2C19 and significantly reduce clopidogrel's antiplatelet activity.
rules.management: Avoid concomitant use (clopidogrel label). If acid suppression is needed, the label notes dexlansoprazole, lansoprazole and pantoprazole had less effect.

sources.label: FDA label: clopidogrel, Drug Interactions: CYP2C19 inhibitors

rules.title: Ketorolac with another NSAID or aspirin
rules.effect: Cumulative risk of serious NSAID adverse effects (bleeding, kidney injury).
rules.management: Contraindicated per the ketorolac label.

rules.title: Simvastatin or lovastatin with gemfibrozil
rules.effect: Myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
rules.management: Contraindicated with simvastatin; avoid with lovastatin.

rules.title: Statin with gemfibrozil
rules.effect: Higher risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
rules.management: Avoid; if a fibrate is needed, fenofibrate interacts less.

rules.title: Simvastatin with verapamil, diltiazem or dronedarone
rules.effect: Higher simvastatin levels; myopathy risk.
rules.management: The simvastatin label says not to exceed 10 mg daily with these drugs.

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)
FDA label: simvastatin, Dosage and Administration

rules.title: Simvastatin with amiodarone, amlodipine or ranolazine
rules.effect: Higher simvastatin levels; myopathy risk.
rules.management: The simvastatin label says not to exceed 20 mg daily with these drugs.

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)
FDA label: simvastatin, Dosage and Administration

rules.title: Lovastatin with verapamil, diltiazem or dronedarone
rules.effect: Higher lovastatin levels; myopathy risk.
rules.management: The lovastatin label says not to exceed 20 mg daily with these drugs.

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)
FDA label: lovastatin, Dosage and Administration

rules.title: Lovastatin with amiodarone
rules.effect: Higher lovastatin levels; myopathy risk.
rules.management: The lovastatin label says not to exceed 40 mg daily with amiodarone.

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)
FDA label: lovastatin, Dosage and Administration

rules.title: Simvastatin or lovastatin with fluconazole
rules.effect: Fluconazole inhibits CYP3A4 and raises simvastatin and lovastatin levels; myopathy and rhabdomyolysis risk (an ONC high-priority pair).
rules.management: Use the lowest statin dose or hold the statin during a short antifungal course; ask about muscle pain or weakness.

sources.label: ONC high-priority drug-drug interactions (Phansalkar et al., JAMIA 2012;19:735-743)

rules.title: Atorvastatin with clarithromycin or itraconazole
rules.effect: Higher atorvastatin levels; myopathy risk.
rules.management: The atorvastatin label says not to exceed 20 mg daily with these drugs.

sources.label: FDA label: atorvastatin, Dosage and Administration

rules.title: Colchicine with a strong CYP3A4 or P-gp inhibitor
rules.effect: Fatal colchicine toxicity has been reported.
rules.management: Contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment; otherwise the colchicine label requires a dose reduction. Prefer another antibiotic or hold colchicine.

sources.label: FDA label: colchicine, Contraindications; Drug Interactions

rules.title: Colchicine with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor
rules.effect: Higher colchicine levels and toxicity.
rules.management: The colchicine label calls for a dose reduction.

rules.title: Ticagrelor with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor
rules.effect: Much higher ticagrelor levels; bleeding.
rules.management: Avoid (ticagrelor label).

rules.title: Ticagrelor with a strong CYP3A4 inducer
rules.effect: Lower ticagrelor levels; loss of effect.
rules.management: Avoid (ticagrelor label).

rules.title: Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir with a contraindicated drug
rules.effect: Ritonavir strongly inhibits CYP3A4: serious or life-threatening reactions with drugs highly dependent on CYP3A4, or loss of antiviral effect with strong inducers.
rules.management: Contraindicated (nirmatrelvir-ritonavir label, section 4). Hold or switch the interacting drug if possible, or choose another COVID-19 treatment.

rules.title: Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir with salmeterol
rules.effect: Higher salmeterol levels: QT prolongation, palpitations and sinus tachycardia.
rules.management: Avoid concomitant use (label); consider a short switch of the inhaler.

rules.title: Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir with quetiapine
rules.effect: Much higher quetiapine levels: sedation, hypotension, QT effects.
rules.management: If co-administration is necessary, the label says to reduce the quetiapine dose and monitor.

rules.title: Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir with an opioid
rules.effect: Higher opioid levels, including potentially fatal respiratory depression (methadone levels may instead fall).
rules.management: Monitor closely and consider reducing the opioid dose (label); for methadone, watch for withdrawal and adjust.

rules.title: Tacrolimus or cyclosporine with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor
rules.effect: Large rise in immunosuppressant levels: nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity.
rules.management: Avoid or monitor levels closely with the transplant team.

rules.title: Tacrolimus or cyclosporine with a strong CYP3A4 inducer
rules.effect: Lower immunosuppressant levels; rejection risk.
rules.management: Avoid or monitor levels closely.

rules.title: Carbamazepine with clarithromycin or erythromycin
rules.effect: Carbamazepine toxicity (ataxia, dizziness, hyponatremia).
rules.management: Prefer azithromycin or another antibiotic; otherwise monitor levels.

rules.title: Eplerenone with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor
rules.effect: Much higher eplerenone levels and hyperkalemia.
rules.management: Contraindicated (eplerenone label).

rules.title: PDE5 inhibitor with a nitrate
rules.effect: Severe, potentially fatal hypotension.
rules.management: Contraindicated. Do not give a nitrate within 24 hours of sildenafil or 48 hours of tadalafil.

rules.title: Riociguat with a PDE5 inhibitor or nitrate
rules.effect: Severe hypotension.
rules.management: Contraindicated (riociguat label).

rules.title: PDE5 inhibitor with an alpha-blocker
rules.effect: Additive blood-pressure lowering; dizziness or fainting.
rules.management: Start the PDE5 inhibitor at the lowest dose once the alpha-blocker is stable.

rules.title: Methotrexate with trimethoprim
rules.effect: Additive folate antagonism and reduced methotrexate clearance: pancytopenia, sometimes fatal.
rules.management: Avoid; choose another antibiotic.

rules.title: Methotrexate with an NSAID
rules.effect: NSAIDs can reduce methotrexate clearance; most serious with high-dose methotrexate.
rules.management: With low-dose weekly methotrexate, monitor blood counts and kidney function.

rules.title: Allopurinol with azathioprine or mercaptopurine
rules.effect: Allopurinol blocks thiopurine breakdown: severe bone-marrow suppression.
rules.management: The allopurinol label calls for reducing the azathioprine or mercaptopurine dose to one-third to one-quarter of usual, with close blood-count monitoring; consider an alternative.

rules.title: Lithium with an NSAID
rules.effect: NSAIDs raise lithium levels: toxicity (tremor, confusion, arrhythmia).
rules.management: Avoid or check lithium levels within about 5 days.

rules.title: Lithium with an ACE inhibitor or ARB
rules.effect: Reduced lithium clearance: toxicity.
rules.management: Monitor lithium levels closely after starting or changing the dose.

rules.title: Lithium with a thiazide diuretic
rules.effect: Thiazides reduce lithium clearance: toxicity.
rules.management: Avoid or monitor lithium levels closely.

rules.title: Digoxin with amiodarone or dronedarone
rules.effect: Higher digoxin levels: bradycardia, heart block, toxicity.
rules.management: The digoxin label advises measuring levels and reducing the digoxin dose when starting these drugs.

rules.title: Digoxin with verapamil or diltiazem
rules.effect: Higher digoxin levels and additive AV-node slowing.
rules.management: Monitor heart rate and digoxin levels.

rules.title: Digoxin with clarithromycin or itraconazole
rules.effect: P-gp inhibition raises digoxin levels.
rules.management: Monitor digoxin levels and symptoms.

rules.title: Dofetilide with a contraindicated drug
rules.effect: Higher dofetilide levels or hypokalemia: torsades de pointes.
rules.management: Contraindicated (dofetilide label).

rules.title: Sacubitril/valsartan with an ACE inhibitor
rules.effect: High risk of angioedema.
rules.management: Contraindicated. Stop the ACE inhibitor at least 36 hours before starting sacubitril/valsartan.

rules.title: Sacubitril/valsartan with an ARB
rules.effect: Sacubitril/valsartan already contains valsartan: duplicate angiotensin blockade.
rules.management: Do not combine (label).

rules.title: ACE inhibitor with an ARB (dual RAAS blockade)
rules.effect: More hyperkalemia, hypotension and acute kidney injury without outcome benefit in most patients.
rules.management: Generally avoid; monitor potassium and creatinine if used.

sources.label: FDA label: lisinopril, Warnings and Precautions: dual blockade

rules.title: Aliskiren with an ACE inhibitor or ARB
rules.effect: Hyperkalemia, hypotension and kidney injury.
rules.management: Contraindicated in patients with diabetes; avoid when eGFR is below 60 (aliskiren label).

rules.title: Amiloride or triamterene with a potassium supplement
rules.effect: Risk of severe, potentially fatal hyperkalemia.
rules.management: Contraindicated (potassium chloride and amiloride labels).

rules.title: Potassium-sparing diuretic with a potassium supplement
rules.effect: Risk of severe hyperkalemia.
rules.management: Avoid potassium supplements unless hypokalemia is documented; check potassium and creatinine.

rules.title: ACE inhibitor or ARB with a potassium-sparing diuretic
rules.effect: Risk of hyperkalemia, especially with reduced kidney function.
rules.management: Check potassium and creatinine within about a week of starting, then periodically.

sources.label: FDA label: spironolactone, Warnings and Precautions: hyperkalemia

rules.title: ACE inhibitor or ARB with a potassium supplement
rules.effect: Risk of hyperkalemia.
rules.management: Confirm the supplement is still needed; check potassium.

rules.title: ACE inhibitor or ARB, potassium-sparing diuretic and potassium supplement together
rules.effect: Three potassium-raising drugs: high risk of life-threatening hyperkalemia.
rules.management: Avoid the potassium supplement unless hypokalemia is documented; check potassium and creatinine promptly.

rules.title: Eplerenone with a potassium supplement or another potassium-sparing diuretic
rules.effect: Hyperkalemia.
rules.management: Contraindicated in hypertension (eplerenone label).

rules.title: Trimethoprim with a potassium-raising drug
rules.effect: Trimethoprim reduces potassium excretion; hyperkalemia, especially in older or kidney-impaired patients.
rules.management: The label says close monitoring of serum potassium is warranted; check potassium during the course.

sources.label: FDA label: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, Warnings and Precautions: hyperkalemia

rules.title: ACE inhibitor or ARB, diuretic and NSAID together
rules.effect: The 'triple whammy': acute kidney injury.
rules.management: Avoid the NSAID if possible; otherwise check creatinine and keep the patient hydrated.

rules.title: Opioid with a benzodiazepine
rules.effect: Profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma and death (FDA boxed warning, 2016).
rules.management: Reserve for patients without alternatives; use the lowest doses and shortest duration, and consider naloxone.

rules.title: Opioid with gabapentin or pregabalin
rules.effect: Serious breathing problems (FDA safety communication, 2019).
rules.management: Start low, monitor for sedation and breathing, consider naloxone.

sources.label: FDA label: gabapentin, Warnings and Precautions: respiratory depression

rules.title: Opioid with a sleep medicine
rules.effect: Additive sedation and respiratory depression.
rules.management: Avoid if possible; use the lowest doses.

rules.title: Opioid with a muscle relaxant
rules.effect: Additive CNS and respiratory depression.
rules.management: Avoid if possible; warn about sedation and driving.

rules.title: Opioid with a sedating antihistamine
rules.effect: Profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma and death (opioid boxed warning: benzodiazepines or other CNS depressants).
rules.management: Avoid if possible, especially in older adults; if used together, use the lowest doses and warn about sedation and falls.

rules.title: Opioid with a CYP3A4 inhibitor
rules.effect: CYP3A4 inhibitors raise levels of these opioids: potentially fatal respiratory depression (boxed warning).
rules.management: Avoid if possible; otherwise monitor closely for sedation and breathing, and consider reducing the opioid dose.

rules.title: Benzodiazepine with a Z-drug
rules.effect: Duplicate sedative effect: falls, confusion, respiratory depression.
rules.management: Avoid combining sedative-hypnotics.

rules.title: Naltrexone with an opioid
rules.effect: Naltrexone blocks opioid analgesia and can precipitate withdrawal.
rules.management: Contraindicated in patients receiving opioid analgesics (naltrexone label).

rules.title: SSRI or SNRI with tramadol
rules.effect: Serotonin syndrome and seizure risk. Fluoxetine and paroxetine also block tramadol's activation (CYP2D6), weakening pain relief.
rules.management: Prefer a non-serotonergic analgesic; if used, start low and teach the warning signs of serotonin syndrome.

sources.label: FDA label: tramadol, Warnings and Precautions: serotonin syndrome

rules.title: SSRI or SNRI with a triptan
rules.effect: Serotonin syndrome has been reported, though rarely.
rules.management: Usually acceptable; counsel on warning signs.

sources.label: FDA label: sumatriptan, Warnings and Precautions

rules.title: SSRI or SNRI with another serotonergic drug
rules.effect: Additive serotonergic effects.
rules.management: Monitor for serotonin syndrome, especially after dose increases.

sources.label: FDA label: sertraline, Warnings and Precautions: serotonin syndrome

rules.title: SSRI with pimozide
rules.effect: Higher pimozide levels and QT prolongation.
rules.management: Contraindicated (SSRI labels: sertraline, citalopram, escitalopram, fluoxetine, paroxetine, fluvoxamine).

rules.title: Fluoxetine, paroxetine or fluvoxamine with thioridazine
rules.effect: CYP2D6 inhibition raises thioridazine levels: QT prolongation and serious arrhythmias.
rules.management: Contraindicated (labels).

rules.title: Cyclobenzaprine with an MAO inhibitor
rules.effect: Hyperpyretic crises, seizures and deaths have occurred.
rules.management: Contraindicated, including within 14 days after stopping an MAOI (cyclobenzaprine label).

rules.title: Cyclobenzaprine with a serotonergic drug
rules.effect: Serotonin syndrome has been reported (cyclobenzaprine label).
rules.management: Watch for agitation, tremor, clonus or fever after starting or raising either drug; consider another muscle relaxant or non-drug measures.

sources.label: FDA label: cyclobenzaprine, Warnings: serotonin syndrome

rules.title: Bupropion with an MAO inhibitor
rules.effect: Hypertensive reactions.
rules.management: Contraindicated; allow 14 days after stopping an MAOI (bupropion label).

rules.title: MAO inhibitor with a decongestant
rules.effect: Hypertensive crisis.
rules.management: Avoid pseudoephedrine and phenylephrine with MAOIs.

rules.title: Tamoxifen with a strong CYP2D6 inhibitor
rules.effect: Less conversion to endoxifen, which may reduce tamoxifen's effect.
rules.management: Prefer an antidepressant with little CYP2D6 inhibition.

rules.title: Ergot with a triptan
rules.effect: Additive vasospasm.
rules.management: Do not use within 24 hours of each other (triptan labels).

rules.title: Two drugs that prolong the QT interval
rules.effect: Additive QT prolongation; torsades risk rises with low potassium or magnesium, bradycardia, heart disease and older age.
rules.management: Consider an alternative to one drug; otherwise check an ECG and electrolytes.

sources.label: FDA label: ondansetron, Warnings and Precautions: QT prolongation
FDA label: azithromycin, Warnings and Precautions: QT prolongation

rules.title: Fluconazole with erythromycin or pimozide
rules.effect: Fluconazole raises levels of these QT-prolonging CYP3A4 substrates: torsades de pointes.
rules.management: Contraindicated (fluconazole label, section 4).

rules.title: Fluoroquinolone with a systemic corticosteroid
rules.effect: Higher risk of tendinitis and tendon rupture, especially over age 60 (boxed warning).
rules.management: Prefer another antibiotic when reasonable; counsel to stop at the first tendon pain.

rules.title: Antibiotic with calcium, iron, magnesium or antacids
rules.effect: Chelation sharply reduces antibiotic absorption.
rules.management: Separate doses (for ciprofloxacin: 2 hours before or 6 hours after).

rules.title: Levothyroxine with calcium, iron or antacids
rules.effect: Reduced levothyroxine absorption.
rules.management: Take levothyroxine at least 4 hours apart from these products.

rules.title: Theophylline with ciprofloxacin or fluvoxamine
rules.effect: Theophylline toxicity: seizures, arrhythmias.
rules.management: Avoid or monitor theophylline levels.

rules.title: Lamotrigine with valproate
rules.effect: Valproate more than doubles lamotrigine levels; higher risk of serious rash.
rules.management: The lamotrigine label has a separate, slower titration for patients on valproate.

sources.label: FDA label: lamotrigine, Dosage and Administration

rules.title: Sulfonylurea or insulin with a fluoroquinolone
rules.effect: Fluoroquinolone labels warn of serious hypoglycemia, including coma, mostly in patients taking oral antidiabetic drugs or insulin.
rules.management: Counsel on hypoglycemia, check glucose more often, and stop the fluoroquinolone if hypoglycemia occurs.

sources.label: FDA label: ciprofloxacin, Warnings and Precautions: blood glucose disturbances
